situation: Half the class did the reading and half clearly did not, and the half that did is getting visibly annoyed at carrying discussions.

dims.SPEAKABILITY: Card 2's lines are shorter and more natural to say aloud, while Card 1's "loaded for this conversation" and the drawn-out four-part structure risk sounding rehearsed.
dims.SPECIFICITY: Both diagnose this exact split-class dynamic well, but Card 2's framing of skipping as self-protection against public exposure is a sharper read of the actual behavior than Card 1's more generic "status wound."
dims.TIGHTNESS: Card 2 does more with fewer words; Card 1's script repeats its "I hold the bar because I know you can clear it" theme in ways that pad the Commitment beat.
dims.HONESTY: Card 1 names the gap more bluntly ("some of you did not"), but Card 2 keeps the standard just as firmly ("I hold all of you to it equally") without publicly outing the unprepared students, which is the harder and better-calibrated move here.
